title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: external address conditions, OR logic and condition testing
summary: Hold: the assurance that administrators need do nothing is not supported by a published government-cloud rollout default. The condition-builder row also presents two role groups as mandatory even though Microsoft documents other administrators with equivalent configuration permissions. The roadmap facts and both control paths are supported.

claims.quote: Message is sent to any of these external email addresses ... | Recipient is | ... Use this condition to detect only messages that are sent outside the organization (messages that cross the firewall).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The government-cloud arrival default and whether existing policies change on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance enhanced policy conditions GCC GCC High DoD condition builder default rollout existing policies. Read roadmap, policies, configure and GCC High planning; found no government-cloud arrival default or existing-policy migration.

claims.claim: Nothing is required of administrators and nothing is forced on them when the government-cloud change arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: "336046" "no action"; Communication Compliance enhanced policy conditions GCC GCC High DoD condition builder default rollout existing policies. Read roadmap, configure, policies and GCC High planning; none states that no administrator action is required on arrival.
claims.fix: Replace 'Nothing is required of administrators; policy authors should plan to review.' with 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival; policy authors should plan to review.' In Why it matters, replace 'The sensible view is that nothing is forced on you, but that' with 'No source says existing policies change;'.

claims.claim: Learn says Communication Compliance usernames are pseudonymized by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Clouds and platform
claims.claim: The cited condition documentation and GCC High planning table do not specify cloud availability for these three enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance enhanced policy conditions GCC GCC High DoD condition builder default rollout existing policies. Read policies, configure and the GCC High deployment table; its Communication Compliance rows do not name OR, external-address conditions or condition testing.

claims.claim: The builder is reached in Microsoft Purview through Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Choose conditions and review percentage > Conditions > Condition builder.
claims.quote: in the Conditions section, above the existing condition builder, turn the Condition builder option on.

claims.claim: The test control is reached in Microsoft Purview through Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Conditions and percentage > Test your conditions.
claims.quote: Select Create policy, then select Custom policy. ... On the Conditions and percentage page, after entering your conditions, select Test your conditions.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation selects the new condition-builder mode for a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance condition builder Test your conditions Microsoft Graph API PowerShell supervisoryReviewRule Condition. Read policies, TCM overview/resources and New-SupervisoryReviewRule; generic Condition syntax does not document selecting the condition-builder mode.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation performs the sample-message condition test.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "test" "conditions" "API" Graph; Communication Compliance condition builder Test your conditions Microsoft Graph API PowerShell supervisoryReviewRule Condition. Read configure, TCM references and New-SupervisoryReviewRule; no test operation found.

claims.claim: Learn says PowerShell is not supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies.
claims.quote: PowerShell isn't supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies. To create and manage these policies, use the policy management controls in the Communication Compliance solution.
claims.fix: After this statement add: 'The Security & Compliance PowerShell reference nevertheless documents New-SupervisoryReviewRule with a Condition parameter for supervisory-review rules; it does not identify a switch for the new condition-builder mode or an operation for sample-message testing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/new-supervisoryreviewrule?view=exchange-ps. Do not infer new-builder support from that reference.

claims.claim: At the time of writing, Learn gives no Microsoft Graph operation that edits Communication Compliance policy conditions.
claims.quote: Searched: "Communication Compliance" "condition builder" "Graph" "conditions". Read TCM overview/resources; documented methods concern monitoring and snapshots, not condition editing.

claims.claim: The TCM Security and Compliance resource reference lists supervisoryReviewRule with a Condition parameter.
claims.quote: supervisoryReviewRule resource type ... Condition | Write | String | The Condition parameter specifies the conditions and exceptions for the rule.

claims.claim: The TCM API overview describes baselines, snapshots, monitoring and drift detection.
claims.quote: Get a baseline and create a snapshot job ... List and get drifts ... Create and manage monitors ... List and get monitoring results ... List, get, and delete snapshot jobs

claims.claim: The TCM references do not say whether supervisoryReviewRule handles new condition-builder conditions.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance condition builder Test your conditions Microsoft Graph API PowerShell supervisoryReviewRule Condition. Read utcm-securityandcompliance-resources supervisoryReviewRule and the TCM API overview; neither specifies new condition-builder compatibility.

claims.claim: Role group membership is configured under Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Role groups ... Select the Communication Compliance role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users
claims.fix: Complete the membership route as 'Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users'. The existing route is correct but stops at the role-group list rather than the membership control.

claims.claim: Role group permissions can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: After configuring your role groups, it might take up to 30 minutes for the role group permissions to apply to assigned users across your organization.

claims.claim: Policy alerts are viewed at Communication Compliance > Alerts.
claims.quote: Sign in to Microsoft 365 as a reviewer designated in the Communication Compliance policy. Go to Communication Compliance > Alerts to view the alerts for your policies.

claims.claim: Learn recommends a pilot tested over several days and is cited as recommending the briefing's small-group pilot.
claims.quote: Typically, you need to create a pilot policy and test it for several days before rolling the policy out to the wider organization.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'Build new policies in the condition builder and start with a pilot policy scoped to a small group. Learn describes testing a pilot for several days before wider rollout.' This keeps the small-group recommendation as the wiki's advice rather than attributing it to Microsoft.

claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to check role-group membership, turn on Quick Summary and review alerts, but those controls have no table rows.
claims.quote: Confirm who holds ... role groups; Turn on Quick Summary; Review alerts in Communication Compliance > Alerts. The controls table has only condition-builder selection and condition testing.
claims.fix: The checklist steps for role-group membership, Quick Summary and Alerts are not represented in the controls table. Remove those three checklist bullets to resolve the mismatch without adding unverified control rows.

claims.claim: The cited billing text does not attach a new charge specifically to these policy-condition enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance condition builder test conditions external addresses licensing price meter. Read configure Subscriptions and billing and plan; billing is described for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, not for selecting OR, external-address conditions or testing sample messages.

claims.claim: The roadmap and cited Learn descriptions do not describe an end-user-facing change introduced by these enhancements.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance enhanced policy conditions GCC GCC High DoD condition builder default rollout existing policies. Read roadmap and policies/configure; enhancements concern policy-authoring and testing, with no stated new scoped-user interface or action.

claims.claim: Learn uses Choose conditions and review percentage for custom policy creation and Conditions and percentage for the test instructions.
claims.quote: On the Choose conditions and review percentage page ... On the Conditions and percentage page, after entering your conditions, select Test your conditions.
